# Devatā Saṁyutta (SN 1)

**ID:** SN 1
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Devatā Saṁyutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Linked Discourses With Deities
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn1

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Devatā Saṁyutta* (or *Devatāsaṁyutta*, "Linked Discourses With Deities") is the opening section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* [SuttaCentral]. The collection depicts the Buddha in dialogue with various deities (*devatā*s), typically opening as an effulgent deity visits the Buddha at night in the monastery at Sāvatthī [SuttaCentral]. The deities in this collection are exclusively male, and while female deities appear elsewhere in Buddhist literature, there is no corresponding *Devīsamyutta* [Williams, Critical Concepts; Skilling, Female Roles]. The visiting devatā poses a question, riddle, challenge, praise, or reflection, which the Buddha answers by elevating the exchange to an ethical or spiritual plane [SuttaCentral; Norman 1983]. Editorial framing across the vaggas varies systematically: the opening discourse provides a narrative introduction describing the setting and the deity's arrival, but subsequent suttas abbreviate or drop the narrative framework entirely, preserving only the verse exchanges [Norman 1983; SuttaCentral]. The verses are predominantly ethical in orientation, often consisting of riddles, question-and-answer pairs, or wordplays [Norman 1983].

While described in traditional thematic overviews as containing 81 discourses, the collection contains 71 individual suttas in the standard digital arrangement, all of which possess known early parallels [SuttaCentral]. Extensive counterparts are preserved in the two Chinese translations of the *Saṁyuktāgama*: the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100, containing 63 parallels) and the main *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, containing 59 parallels), with additional parallels found in Sanskrit fragments (such as SHT Sutta 41 to SN 1.27) and the *Mahāprajñāpāramitopadeśa* (T 1509) [SuttaCentral]. Cross-language machine alignments by DharmaNexus corroborate extensive passage sharing with T 99 and T 100, and further identify shared verse sequences in the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* and *Mahāsamājasūtra*, as well as Tibetan canonical texts such as the *Mahāsamaya-sūtra* (D0034, D0653) and *Tridharmaka-sūtra* (D0253) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus records over 6,000 reuse matches across 270 texts, most notably with the adjacent *Devaputta Saṁyutta* (SN 2), multiple *nipāta*s of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, and the *Mahāsamaya Sutta* of the *Dīghanikāya* (DN 20) [DharmaNexus].
